title: Build a min-priority queue in Python wrapping heapq
description: Greenfield Python task: implement MinPriorityQueue wrapping heapq with push(item, priority), pop() -> item, peek() -> item, is_empty(), and __len__. Lower priority number = higher priority. Raises IndexError on pop/peek of empty queue.

injections.content:
import pytest
from src.priority_queue import MinPriorityQueue


def test_push_pop_order():
    pq = MinPriorityQueue()
    pq.push("low", 10)
    pq.push("high", 1)
    pq.push("mid", 5)
    assert pq.pop() == "high"   # priority 1 comes first
    assert pq.pop() == "mid"    # priority 5
    assert pq.pop() == "low"    # priority 10


def test_peek_does_not_remove():
    pq = MinPriorityQueue()
    pq.push("x", 3)
    pq.push("y", 1)
    assert pq.peek() == "y"
    assert len(pq) == 2


def test_is_empty():
    pq = MinPriorityQueue()
    assert pq.is_empty()
    pq.push("a", 1)
    assert not pq.is_empty()


def test_len():
    pq = MinPriorityQueue()
    pq.push("a", 1)
    pq.push("b", 2)
    assert len(pq) == 2
    pq.pop()
    assert len(pq) == 1


def test_pop_empty_raises():
    pq = MinPriorityQueue()
    with pytest.raises(IndexError):
        pq.pop()


def test_peek_empty_raises():
    pq = MinPriorityQueue()
    with pytest.raises(IndexError):
        pq.peek()


def test_equal_priority_stable():
    pq = MinPriorityQueue()
    pq.push("first", 5)
    pq.push("second", 5)
    # Both have same priority; either order is acceptable
    result = {pq.pop(), pq.pop()}
    assert result == {"first", "second"}

task_spec.prompt:
Implement MinPriorityQueue in src/priority_queue.py.

import heapq

class MinPriorityQueue:
    def __init__(self)
    def push(self, item, priority: int | float)  # push item with given priority
    def pop(self)           # remove and return item with lowest priority; raise IndexError if empty
    def peek(self)          # view item with lowest priority without removing; raise IndexError if empty
    def is_empty(self) -> bool
    def __len__(self) -> int

Use heapq internally. Store tuples of (priority, counter, item) to handle equal priorities.

All 7 tests in tests/test_pq.py must pass.
Run: uv run pytest tests/ -v
required_artifacts: push stores (priority, counter, item) tuples for stability
pop removes and returns item with lowest priority
IndexError raised on pop/peek of empty queue
